name: Abraha
tagline: He marched on the Kaaba with elephants. Allah sent small birds.
description: Watch the fall of Abraha, scene by scene: the cathedral in Sana'a, the march on Makkah with elephants, Abd al-Muttalib's camels, the elephant that would not move, the birds in flocks, and the year the Prophet ﷺ was born. Told through Surah al-Fil and the Sirah of Ibn Ishaq.
outro: Let them worship the Lord of this House.

lines: Abraha ruled Yemen for the king of Abyssinia.
In Sana'a he built a great cathedral,
and wanted the Arabs to make their pilgrimage there instead of the Kaaba.
When the Arabs refused, he marched on Makkah to tear the Kaaba down.
A great army, with a war elephant at its head.
The tribes who stood in his way were scattered.
His men seized the camels of Makkah, two hundred of them Abd al-Muttalib's.
Abd al-Muttalib came to Abraha and asked only for his camels.
Abraha was surprised: not a word for the House of your fathers?
"I am the lord of the camels," he said.
"The House has a Lord who will protect it."
Then the people of Makkah left for the hills, and waited.
At dawn the elephant was turned toward Makkah.
It knelt, and would not rise.
Turned toward Yemen, it got up and ran.

hadith.text: When the Prophet's camel knelt near Makkah at al-Hudaybiyyah, he said: "She was held back by the One who held back the elephant."
hadith.cite: Sahih al-Bukhari, the story of al-Hudaybiyyah

lines: Then birds came in from the sea, flock after flock.
Each carried three small stones: one in its beak, two in its claws.
No bigger than a lentil.
Whoever they struck did not survive.
The army broke and fled down the road it came by.
Abraha was struck too. He died soon after reaching Sana'a.
The Arabs named it the Year of the Elephant.
That same year in Makkah, a child was born:
Muhammad ﷺ.
He trusted the biggest animal on earth.
Allah answered with some of the smallest.
The House he came to destroy still stands.
